prompt:
以下はある英語ニュースpodcast記事のFull Story・Point One・Point Twoです。
Point One・Point Twoそれぞれについて、以下6項目を判定してください
(それぞれPASS/FAIL)。

- qa_not_caveat_only: このPointが、研究上の限界・一般化上の注意・免責事項
  だけで構成されていない場合PASS(それらに加えて実質的な新しい内容がある
  場合もPASS。留保だけでPoint枠全体が終わっている場合はFAIL)
- qa_not_full_story_paraphrase: Full Storyの要約・言い換えに留まっていない
  場合PASS(Full Storyの中心的なlogic・結論を語彙だけ変えて繰り返している
  場合はFAIL)
- qa_not_other_point_paraphrase: もう一方のPointの要約・言い換えになって
  いない場合PASS
- qa_explains_why_it_matters: 「だから何なのか」を具体的に説明できている
  場合PASS(聞き手にとっての具体的な意味・示唆がある場合)
- qa_specific_not_generic: この記事のLedger固有の内容に基づいており、他の
  どんな記事にもほぼそのまま流用できる一般論になっていない場合PASS
- qa_adds_new_value: 新しい理解・解釈・意外性・具体的示唆のいずれかを
  実際に加えている場合PASS(Full Storyだけを聞いた場合と比べて、聞き手の
  理解が実際に深まっている場合)

reasoningには、判定理由を1〜2文の日本語で書いてください(特にFAILの場合は
具体的な理由を明記してください)。

【Full Story】
As of September 2026, the interesting change in Japanese travel may not be that trips are getting longer. It may be that young travelers want more control over their time during a trip.

Several surveys point in this direction, especially for young men. In one 2025 survey, men aged 29 and under most often chose solo travel, at about 25%, or travel built around a hobby. These choices suggest a trip built around the traveler’s own interests and time.

Another survey tells the same story. About 90% of Japanese Gen Z respondents aged 19 to 25 said they wanted free time during an overseas tour. Most of that group wanted half a day or more. The wish is clear: even inside a planned tour, they want room to choose their own pace.

But the calendar tells a different story.

In one survey, people were asked what they would do if they could take one month off. The most common answer was a trip of about one week, chosen by about 24%.

In a separate autumn survey, people planning a trip expected to stay for an average of less than two nights. The middle answer was two nights.

This gap matters. The surveys show a clear wish for slower, more personal travel. But longer stays have not yet become common. Japan’s Tourism White Paper also lists longer stays as a policy task.

So this is not a completed move from sightseeing to slow travel. It is a change in preference, while short travel plans remain strong.

【Point One】
A traveler can take only two nights and still protect half a day with no group schedule. They can travel alone or build the trip around a hobby. The first change may be control over time, not a longer calendar. Length alone may miss part of the story.

【Point Two】
There is no single young Japanese traveler here. Among men aged 29 and under, solo travel was about 25%, and hobby-focused travel was also a leading choice. Among women the same age, visiting famous tourist sites was still about 45%. The shift is strongest in one group, not all young people.

point_one.reasoning: 短期旅行でも自由時間を確保できるという実用的な読みは示すが、Full Storyの中心結論である「滞在日数ではなく時間の主導権が変化している」をほぼ言い換えている。Half day、二泊、ソロ旅行や趣味旅行も本文の情報の再構成にとどまり、実質的な新規価値は弱い。

point_two.reasoning: 若年層全体を一括りにせず、29歳以下の男性と女性で旅行志向が異なることを、女性の有名観光地志向約45%という具体的な比較で示している。したがって、変化が若者全体に均等に広がっているわけではないという重要な限定と解釈が加わっている。
